payload.summary: Since August 2026, dispute ticket volume has roughly doubled (from ~600/month in Jun-Jul to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep, E-07). A significant driver is billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), which compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling; firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report registers in 0.1 m3 units rather than m3 (E-13), so BV-17 misclassifies their normal consumption as high and rejects the read (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) at billing import, forcing estimate substitution. proposal.summary: The problem began as a stakeholder request (CL-01, SH-CS): dispute tickets had doubled since August, and Customer Service wanted an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix wrong bills — a framing to be tested, not a given fact. Evidence confirmed the doubling (E-07: ~600/month to 1180-1260/month from Aug-Sep 2026). An initial problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributing the surge mainly to ACTUAL-read bill errors was invalidated by E-11 and superseded by PD-1@v2. Investigation then established a confirmed mechanism for the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset: billing-import rule BV-17 (E-12, deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw AMI register values to m3 history without converting firmware v4.2's 0.1-m3 units (E-13), causing valid reads to be wrongly rejected as high-consumption — accounting for 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-11, E-14). However, the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population (1785 of 3025, 59%, per E-03) has no confirmed cause, and the related verification obligation remains open. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no holds): the released scope is limited to read-only billing-rule investigation, AMI read-event investigation, and dispute-volume monitoring, with no automated bill writes and no ticket-auto-answering agent, consistent with the no-automated-writes constraint. Several known limitations and open verification obligations are carried forward rather than resolved, and one limitation statement in the release itself was flagged as inconsistent with the underlying data-asset records.
